evidence.activity: Starter Suite, an all-in-one business software product built for small and medium-size businesses

evidence.section: Item 1 > Other Salesforce Offerings > Salesforce Starter

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: business software built for small businesses, with no user or revenue figures

evidence.activity: AppExchange marketplace where independent software vendors and third-party developers market and sell their applications

evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Business and Growth Strategy > Leverage our partner ecosystem

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: seller marketplace for independent software vendors, with no seller counts disclosed

creativity.reason: Level 1: the only creative work is original Salesforce+ programming used as a routine marketing input, while the core CRM, data and AI software does not create or enable creative work as the rubric defines it.

community.reason: Level 2: specific current activities (employee development, donation matching, paid volunteer time off and customer/partner certification courses) with no reach figures such as participants or total dollars, so substantial reach is not shown.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1 based on general language only (equality values and equal-opportunity compliance boilerplate); coverage is insufficient under condition 3, because the filing refers readers to its Stakeholder Impact Report for workforce information and describes no specific inclusion activities itself.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 2: specific current enabling offerings (Starter Suite small-business software and the AppExchange seller marketplace), but no figures on users, sellers or revenue.

ai.notes: The Item 7 (targeted) excerpt was empty, so scoring rests on Item 1 only. Cross-cultural coverage is insufficient (condition 3: the filing refers to the Stakeholder Impact Report at salesforce.com, which is on the main domain), so this triggers the automated second look. Excluded as traps or non-qualifying: Trailhead described as free resources to help companies learn our systems and reduce attrition, and Salesforce+ educational content listed under marketing (both educating customers as marketing); AI generation of marketing 'content' and product descriptions ('content' trap); 'collaboration' as a product feature; strategic investments in technology startups (the company's own financial and strategic investing, not a program aimed at founder barriers); 'innovation' language; 'foundation' used as a metaphor. The 'community of tens of millions of Trailblazers' is a user and developer community figure, not tied to a specific education or community-investment program, so it was not used as an indicator. The E7 marketplace serves ISVs whose size is not disclosed. E5 certification courses are part of professional services with no revenue disclosed, so they were tagged external_education at level 2 rather than education_business.
